title: App Store IAP price snapshot (SA/AE/EG/US) of 21 comparable apps — mystery games, interactive story, Arabic edutainment, audio/reading subscriptions, 2026-10-27
authors: ATHAR W2-BUSINESS team (data capture from Apple App Store pages and iTunes Lookup API)
publisher: Apple Inc. (App Store public product pages)
key_findings: Golden Idol (mobile) is free-to-start with one 'Unlock Full Game' IAP: SAR 20.99 / AED 25.99 / EGP 169.00 / US$6.99 — a premium-unlock model priced at about half its Steam price in the same storefront (SAR 39.99; ratio 1.9x). [Corrected/Clarified 2026-10-27 by deep-card review]
Arabic edutainment subscriptions cluster at SAR 25-40/month: I Read Arabic SAR 24.99/mo; 3asafeer SAR 39.99/mo or SAR 349.99/yr; Lamsa SAR 14.99-59.99/mo, SAR 129.99-269.99/yr.

Arabic reading/audio subscriptions: Abjjad SAR 36.49/mo, SAR 349.99/yr (US$14.99/mo on US store); Wajeez SAR 20.99-34.99/mo, SAR 204.99/yr; Rufoof SAR 29.99/mo, SAR 299.99/yr; Storytel 'Unlimited (SA)' SAR 34.99/mo, SAR 299.99/yr.
Interactive-story F2P apps sell VIP subscriptions at SAR 59.99-64.99/month (Choices VIP SAR 59.99; Episode VIP Sapphire SAR 64.99) and currency packs from SAR 4.99 to SAR 399.99.

Egypt storefront prices are far lower in USD terms for subscriptions set per-region (e.g., Storytel Unlimited (Egypt) EGP 89.99/mo; Anghami Plus Egypt EGP 69.99) — evidence that serious regional apps set Egypt-specific tiers.
athar_applications: Primary price anchors for ATHAR's B2C family plan and per-case unlocks in the Gulf (see BUSINESS_MODEL_AND_PRICING_EVIDENCE.md §2 and pricing_benchmarks.csv).
Supports a two-tier regional price (Gulf vs Egypt/Levant) rather than one global price.
limitations: App Store pages list at most ~10 IAP items; labels do not always state the billing period; prices are snapshots and change; not a measure of sales or conversion.
Rating counts per storefront are small for several apps; App Store reflects higher-income iOS users, not Android-heavy Egypt/Morocco.

title: Steam regional price snapshot via Storefront appdetails API (SA/AE/EG/US): Golden Idol, Rise of the Golden Idol, Obra Dinn, Her Story, Shadows of Doubt — 2026-10-27
authors: ATHAR W2-BUSINESS team (data capture from Steam Storefront API)
key_findings: Saudi storefront (SAR): Golden Idol 39.99; Rise of the Golden Idol 40.95; Obra Dinn 40.95 list (27.43 on 33% sale); Her Story 22.49; Shadows of Doubt 51.49.
UAE storefront (AED): Golden Idol 50.00; Rise 53.00; Obra Dinn 53.00 list; Her Story 29.00; Shadows of Doubt 66.00.
Egypt is served in USD at roughly half the US price: Golden Idol $9.29 vs $17.99 US; Obra Dinn $10.49 vs $19.99 US; Shadows of Doubt $12.49 vs $24.99 US — a publisher-accepted ~50% regional discount.
athar_applications: Upper bound for a one-off premium Arabic case collection on PC/web (SAR ~22-51); confirms that premium detective games keep Gulf prices near US parity but discount Egypt by about half.
limitations: Snapshot prices; sale prices fluctuate; Steam is PC-only and adult-skewed; no sales volumes.

limitations: App Store pages list at most ~10 IAP items; labels do not always state the billing period; prices are snapshots and change; not a measure of sales or conversion.
Billing period of VIP not stated on the page (assumed monthly by convention; not verified).

title: Episode - Choose Your Story — App Store listing (SA/AE/EG/US) VIP and currency prices

title: Storytel - Audiobooks Library — App Store listing (SA/AE/EG/US) regional 'Unlimited' plans
key_findings: Region-named SKUs: Unlimited (SA) SAR 34.99 / US$7.99; Unlimited (UAE) AED 37.99 / US$9.99; Unlimited (Egypt) EGP 89.99 / US$5.49; Unlimited 1Y (SA) SAR 299.99; 1Y (Egypt) EGP 709.00.
The storytel.com UAE site separately shows $9.99/mo, $53.64/6 months, $83.88/yr (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Audio-first test (KO-PO-08B-001) price anchor: Arabic audiobook unlimited ≈ SAR 35/mo in KSA, ≈ EGP 90 in Egypt.

title: Audible: Audiobooks & Podcasts — App Store listing (SA/AE/EG) plan SKUs
key_findings: App is downloadable in SA/AE/EG, but all SKUs are tied to foreign marketplaces (US/UK/CA/AU), e.g., 'US Premium Monthly' SAR 62.99-69.99, 'US Plus Monthly' SAR 32.99; no Saudi/Emirati/Egyptian marketplace SKU appears.
Interpretation: no local Audible marketplace or Arabic catalogue is evidenced in these storefronts (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Arabic audio subscription competition comes from Storytel, Abjjad, Wajeez, Rufoof — not Audible.
limitations: App Store pages list at most ~10 IAP items; labels do not always state the billing period; prices are snapshots and change; not a measure of sales or conversion.
Absence of a local marketplace inferred from SKU names; not confirmed by an Audible statement.

title: Anghami — App Store listing (SA/AE/EG/US) Anghami Plus plans including student and Egypt tiers
key_findings: Anghami Plus SAR 22.99 / AED 22.99; 'for Students' SAR 11.99 (≈50% off); Family AED 34.49; Egypt 'Plus Egypt, no trial' EGP 69.99 and family EGP 104.99.
230,372 ratings in SA and 501,146 in EG (2026-10-27) — scale reference for a regional subscription brand.
athar_applications: Precedent for explicit student pricing (~50%) and Egypt-specific tiers in a MENA consumer subscription.

title: Noon Academy — App Store listing (SA/US) course and package prices
key_findings: Saudi exam-prep products: 'Noon Plus Package' SAR 117.99-294.99; Qudurat programmes SAR 294.99-399.99; comprehensive Qudurat foundation course SAR 1,199.99; Tahsili courses SAR 669.00.
athar_applications: Saudi families pay SAR 100-1,200 for high-stakes exam prep; ATHAR's critical-thinking product is not high-stakes and should not expect that willingness to pay unless linked to Qudurat-style outcomes (which it must not claim without evidence).
limitations: App Store pages list at most ~10 IAP items; labels do not always state the billing period; prices are snapshots and change; not a measure of sales or conversion.

title: Breakout EDU — Pricing page (Single Classroom and School/District plans)
key_findings: Single Classroom: 'starting at $99/year' for 1 educator and up to 60 students; price preview by number of educators (1 to 6+).

School or District: 'starting at $1,499/year' for all students and educators, with admin usage dashboard, SSO, professional development and a dedicated success manager; price preview by number of schools (1, 2-5, 6-10, 10+).
athar_applications: Closest priced analogue to ATHAR's teacher/class licence (mystery/escape games for class); gives a per-teacher ($99/yr) and per-school ($1,499/yr) US anchor.
limitations: US list prices 'starting at'; actual quotes vary by size; no Arabic content; no efficacy evidence on page.

title: Legends of Learning — Pricing page (Premium Classroom and School plans)
key_findings: Premium Classroom: $790 per year per teacher (5E lesson plans, reporting, unlimited assignments).
School plan: $4,450 for a 400-1,000-student school (price selector by school size); 'Learning Universe' of 2k+ games made by professional studios; district pricing by request.
athar_applications: Upper anchor for a full-featured per-teacher game-based licence ($790/yr) and a per-school licence (~$4.45k/yr for 400-1,000 students ≈ $4.45-11 per student).
limitations: US prices; maths/science only; per-student equivalent is our calculation.

title: Kahoot! — Plans for schools and teachers (Kahoot!+ Bronze/Silver/Gold, Kahoot! One)
key_findings: Free tier (Kahoot! Go); Kahoot!+ Bronze $3/month billed annually ($36/yr; 50 participants); Silver $7/month ($84/yr; 100 participants); Gold $12/month ($144/yr; 200 participants); Kahoot! One $19/month ($228/yr).
Monthly billing options are higher ($9, $15, $26 per month for Bronze/Silver/Gold).
athar_applications: Shows teacher-paid (out-of-pocket) price ceiling for a classroom tool: $36-228/yr — relevant if ATHAR offers a teacher self-serve tier before school procurement.
limitations: US-dollar list prices; not a mystery product; currency selector exists but regional prices not captured.

title: Genially — Pricing (Free, Pro, Master, Author plans)
key_findings: Free plan €0; Pro €6/month billed annually; Master €20/member/month billed annually; Author €40/member/month billed annually (SCORM export, translation AI).
Free tier includes 1,000+ templates; AI credits scale with plan (500 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 per year).
athar_applications: Teachers can already author escape-room activities free in Genially; ATHAR's paid value must be curated, reviewed Arabic cases plus assessment, not templates.
limitations: Individual/team pricing; education-specific plans not captured; euro list prices.

title: Kialo Edu — 'Why it's free' pricing page
key_findings: Kialo Edu states it is free 'forever' with no ads, operated as a nonprofit and funded entirely by a private philanthropic foundation since 2011.
Claims about a million people use it.
athar_applications: A free, well-regarded argument-mapping competitor caps what schools will pay for 'argument' features alone; ATHAR must price the cases + assessment, not the argument tool.
limitations: Self-reported usage; no Arabic interface evidenced.

title: State of Subscription Apps 2026 (RevenueCat)
key_findings: Sample: 115,000+ apps, $16B+ revenue, 1B+ transactions on RevenueCat's platform; target period 2025; MEA region = Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Turkey, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya.

Education: median D30 download-to-trial 6.5%; median monthly price $9.99 and yearly $44.99 (highest of all categories); median realized LTV per payer after year 1 $22.82; 78.5% of trials start on day 0.

All apps: D35 download-to-paid median 2.0% (hard paywall 10.7%, freemium 2.1%); trial-to-paid median 25.5% (≤4-day trials), 37.4% (5-9 days), 42.5% (17-32 days); year-1 retention median 28% (annual plans), 8% (monthly), ~1% (weekly); 6-month retention of monthly plans 14-26% by category.

MEA: trial-to-paid median ~19.5% vs 34.2% North America; 63.5% of conversions on day 0; plan mix 52-55% monthly (highest of any region) and lowest yearly share; median MRR growth -9.7% (only negative region).
Gaming: trial-to-paid median 25.0%; D35 download-to-paid median 1.0% (top quartile 2.3%); monthly median $4.99; 82% weekly plans.
athar_applications: Primary sourced inputs for UNIT_ECONOMICS_SCENARIOS.md (conversion, retention, LTV); MEA-specific trial-to-paid and monthly-plan preference argue for monthly + annual family plans with a 7-day trial.
limitations: Vendor dataset (apps using RevenueCat only; selection bias toward subscription-first apps); some internal inconsistencies across sections (e.g., monthly median $8 vs $9.99); no Education x MEA cross-tab; RLTV definition 'net value' — net of store fees not explicitly stated.

title: 2025 Mobile Gaming Benchmarks (GameAnalytics)
key_findings: Covers 2024 data from ~11,600 apps across 9 regions, 2 platforms and 16 genres (classic retention).
Top-25% D1 retention 26.48-27.69%; median D7 3.42-3.94%; 75% of games below 3% at D28.
Middle East leads median retention on every horizon: D1 22.64%, D7 4.91%, D28 1.49%.
Board, card, puzzle and casino genres show the best medium/long-term retention.
athar_applications: Retention priors for B2C funnel modelling; MENA players retain slightly better than global medians.
limitations: Platform-customer sample (GameAnalytics SDK users), skewed to casual/hyper-casual; no narrative-mystery breakdown; no monetization metrics.

title: 2026 Mobile & PC Gaming Benchmarks (GameAnalytics)
key_findings: Mobile retention kept sliding in 2025: median D1 ≈22%, D7 just under 4%, D30 ≈0.7-0.8%; top 1% hold 64-68% D1 and 13-15% D30.
Median mobile game gets ~12 min daily playtime, ~3.1-3.5 min sessions and ~3.8 sessions/day (16,262 games with ≥1,000 MAU per gamedevreports summary).
athar_applications: A 30-45 minute case is far above median mobile session length — design and pricing should assume multi-session completion and school-time play.
limitations: Aggregated across genres; vendor sample; MENA figures for 2025 not stated on the page.

title: Moloco: 2025 State of Mobile Gaming — In-App Purchase (press release, 15 Apr 2025)
key_findings: Top 5% of US iOS high-value users (0.02% of global installs) generate 20% of global gaming IAP revenue (press release).
Report summary (gamedevreports): top 5% / 10% / 25% of payers generate 48% / 64% / 77% of global IAP revenue; sample = 100 top-grossing publishers, 24 months, 4B installs, $8B IAP.
athar_applications: F2P IAP revenue depends on heavy spenders — incompatible with ATHAR's no-paid-hints/no-currency policy for minors (R9); supports a flat subscription/licence model.
limitations: Advertising-platform vendor; top-grossing publishers only; no MENA breakdown.

title: Adjust Gaming App Insights Report 2026 (via PPC Land and gamedevreports summaries)
key_findings: Gaming CPI rose globally to $0.56 in 2025 (+30% YoY); CPM $4.34; median paid/organic install ratio 3.33 (from 2.07).
MENA was the only region with gaming install growth (+2%) and sessions +7% in 2025; global D1 retention 27%.
Data: top 5,000 apps and Adjust dataset, Jan 2024-Jan 2026, 23 genres, 6 regions, 21 countries.
athar_applications: Global gaming CPI is a floor, not a forecast, for ATHAR acquisition costs (teen-safe targeting and parental-consent funnels will cost more); used only as a labelled sensitivity input.
limitations: Secondary summaries of a gated report (official Adjust page returned 429); global CPI blends hyper-casual; no MENA CPI given.

title: AppsFlyer: Ramadan effect — Middle East mobile app IAP revenue surpasses US$1.7 billion (press release, 2 Apr 2025)
key_findings: Ramadan 2025: in-app purchase revenue +18.6% YoY to US$1.70B across UAE, KSA, Qatar, Egypt and Jordan (800+ apps with ≥1,000 daily installs per country; 220M installs).
Gaming non-organic installs -1% regionally; gaming sessions flat (+0.05%); shopping non-organic installs +76%.
athar_applications: Ramadan is a strong consumer-spend window for paid apps in the Gulf but not for paid gaming installs; schedule B2C promotions around Ramadan/Eid with caution.
limitations: Vendor data; categories limited to shopping, finance, gaming; Ramadan-only window.

title: Payment methods that you can use with your Apple Account (Apple Support, HT202631/111741)
key_findings: Mobile phone billing for Apple purchases (page dated 7 Aug 2026): Saudi Arabia — Mobily, STC, Zain; UAE — du, Etisalat; Egypt — Vodafone; Kuwait — Ooredoo, STC, Zain; Qatar — Ooredoo, Vodafone; Bahrain — Beyon, STC, Zain Bahrain; Oman — Omantel, Ooredoo, Vodafone.
No carrier billing listed for Jordan, Lebanon or Morocco (cards only); Apple Pay listed for the UAE among these countries.
athar_applications: In-app subscriptions can already be carrier-billed in KSA/UAE/Egypt without an operator deal — B2B2C telco partnerships are a distribution, not a payment, necessity there; Jordan/Lebanon/Morocco lack this rail.
limitations: Carrier list subject to change; does not show usage share.

title: App Store Small Business Program (Apple Developer)
key_findings: Reduced commission of 15% on paid apps and In-App Purchases for developers with up to US$1 million in proceeds in the prior calendar year (and new developers).
If proceeds exceed US$1M in the current year, the standard rate applies to future sales.
athar_applications: Unit-economics input: iOS net = price excl. VAT × 85% while under $1M proceeds.
limitations: Enrolment required; standard rate (30%, and 15% for subscriptions after year one) is not restated on this page.

title: Google Play Console Help — Service fees
key_findings: Markets outside AU/EEA/JP/UK/US (i.e., MENA) until the new fee model rolls out: 15% on the first US$1M of annual earnings for developers enrolled in the 15% tier, 30% above; automatically renewing subscriptions 15% regardless of earnings.
New model already live in EEA/UK/US (30 Jun 2026) and AU/JP (30 Sep 2026): e.g., subscriptions 10% + 5% billing fee.
athar_applications: Unit-economics input: Android subscriptions in MENA net 85% of the tax-exclusive price.
limitations: Fee model is changing by region; MENA timing of the new model not stated.

title: Zain KSA — Carrier billing now available for App Store, Apple Music & iTunes purchases (31 Aug 2016)
key_findings: From 30 Aug 2016 Zain Saudi Arabia customers could select Carrier Billing as the payment method for App Store, Apple Music and iTunes purchases, with one-tap purchase.

Related: Boku announced Zain KSA direct carrier billing for Google Play on 14 May 2015 (App Developer Magazine), citing World Bank figures that ~17% of Saudis held a credit card and 46% a bank account at the time.
athar_applications: Historical evidence that Saudi telcos have long offered store carrier billing — reduces the payment barrier for teen-adjacent family purchases.
limitations: Old announcement; banking-penetration figures dated (pre-2015) and superseded by later financial inclusion.

title: Vodafone Egypt — Edu bundle ('PLUS Students' line for Ministry education tablets)
key_findings: EGP 5/month bundle with 1 GB usable only on Ministry of Education websites and apps on the ministry-issued secondary-school tablet; SIM locked to that tablet; offered 'in collaboration' with the Ministry.
Free SIM (instead of EGP 85); auto-renews every 30 days.
athar_applications: In Egypt, telco education data is zero-rated only for ministry-approved content on ministry tablets — inclusion requires Ministry/EKB approval, not a telco deal alone.
limitations: Does not list which platforms are whitelisted; date of offer launch not shown.

title: UAE Ministry of Finance — Federal Supplier Register (Digital Procurement Platform)
authors: Ministry of Finance, United Arab Emirates
key_findings: Registration in the Federal Supplier Register is the first step to bid for federal entities; eligible categories explicitly include free-zone companies, SMEs, freelancers and foreign companies based outside the UAE.

Steps: registration (trade licence number, tax status, licensing authority) → qualification (bank details, documents) → activation; approval up to 30 working days (page also claims one working day); annual renewal; approved suppliers can list products in the DPP e-catalogue.
athar_applications: An IFZA (Dubai free-zone) company is eligible to register to sell to federal bodies such as the UAE Ministry of Education (MoE tenders run on this unified platform).
limitations: Registration ≠ award; MoE public-school content is concentrated with Alef (ATH-SRC-1515); no fee information on page.

title: UAE Ministry of Education — Procurement page
authors: Ministry of Education, United Arab Emirates
key_findings: MoE publishes tenders on the unified digital procurement platform for federal entities; suppliers must be registered and qualified with the Ministry of Finance before bidding.
Links a supplier registration manual and participation manual; no thresholds or free-zone conditions stated.
athar_applications: Confirms the federal route (MoF register → MoE tenders) for UAE public-sector sales.
limitations: Page lacks dates, thresholds and document lists.

title: ADEK (Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge) — Suppliers page
authors: Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge
key_findings: Suppliers register via the Abu Dhabi government supplier portal (supplier.adgpg.gov.ae) to enter ADEK's supplier database; ADEK may request more information at pre-qualification; registration does not guarantee business.
Invoices are submitted through I-Supplier; vendor-management contact suppliers@adek.gov.ae.
athar_applications: Abu Dhabi is a separate emirate-level procurement route from federal MoE; ADEK's public-school platform is already contracted to Alef (ATH-SRC-1515).
limitations: Eligibility criteria (e.g., Abu Dhabi licence) not stated on the page.

title: National eLearning Center (Saudi Arabia) — eLearning Implementing (Executive) Rules
key_findings: Art. 7: government, private and non-profit entities, local or international, must obtain a licence before starting eLearning activity that provides education or training through eLearning in the Kingdom and grants completion certificates.

Art. 8 licence types: programme/curriculum (blended or distance) and programme/training course (blended or distance); Art. 9 conditions include licences from relevant Saudi authorities, meeting Center standards, fees and technical linkage to the National eLearning Platform.
Board approval Decision No. 46/17/6 dated 11/5/1446H (≈ Nov 2024); page last updated 21 Sep 2026.
athar_applications: If ATHAR sells certified courses (e.g., a 'critical-thinking certificate') in KSA it likely needs an NeLC licence; an enrichment game without certificates may fall outside Art. 7 — needs Saudi legal opinion (G01).
limitations: The rules do not address K-12 enrichment content explicitly; validity period not stated; interpretation requires local counsel.

title: Coordinating the State's Knowledge Project: the Egyptian Knowledge Bank (chapter 19 in Education 2.0: Chronicles of Technological and Cultural Change in Egypt)
key_findings: EKB launched January 2016; content from named publishers (Discovery Education, Britannica, Pearson, Nahdet Misr, Wolfram, etc.), each in its own 'sandbox'; a private firm (LIMS) coordinates the platform.

Each publisher signs a protocol with the Ministry of Education (MOETE) on learning objectives; publishers quoted either a one-time perpetual licence or an annual subscription per content type — i.e., central state licensing, not school-by-school sales.
Interview-reported usage (Mar 2020): ~1.6M daily users; planned LMS for 22M+ students in 50,000+ schools.
athar_applications: Egypt's institutional route is a central content licence to the state platform (EKB) — requires an Arabic-curriculum fit and a ministry protocol, not individual school sales.
limitations: Interview-based figures from 2020; current EKB onboarding procedures not documented.

title: Jordan Country Commercial Guide — Selling to the Public Sector (U.S. International Trade Administration)
authors: U.S. Department of Commerce, International Trade Administration
key_findings: Jordan's online e-procurement system is JONEPS, used by the General Supplies Department and the Government Tenders Directorate; Jordan has not signed the WTO Government Procurement Agreement.
Foreign firms may bid on tenders open to international bidders; donor-funded projects (World Bank, EBRD) follow donor procurement rules; a local partner is recommended. Last published 26 Feb 2026.
athar_applications: In Jordan the realistic paid route is donor-funded programmes (media and information literacy with UNESCO/JMI) rather than MoE tenders.
limitations: US-government guide; no education-specific procedure; no local-preference percentage stated.

title: KHDA: Dubai schools to add 18,000 affordable seats as student numbers climb to 406,563 (Gulf News, 1 Oct 2026)
key_findings: KHDA figures: 406,563 students in Dubai private schools at the start of 2026-27 (vs ~388,731 in June 2026, +4.6%).
26 new private institutions opened this year (7 schools, 17 early-childhood centres, 2 HE institutions); ~18,000 affordable seats planned over two years.
athar_applications: Bottom-up sizing input: Dubai private-school market is ~407k students, all reachable by school-level purchasing (no ministry tender needed).
limitations: Journalistic report of KHDA data; grade/curriculum breakdown and Arabic-medium share not given.

title: NCLE says private education in Saudi at 16.5% (Argaam, 7 Jul 2024)
key_findings: The chairman of the National Company for Learning & Education (NCLE) stated private education reached an all-time high of 16.5% of total enrolment in Saudi Arabia (2024).
athar_applications: Combined with MoE totals (ATH-SRC-1556), gives an [استنتاج استثماري] estimate of the Saudi private-school intermediate/secondary population for bottom-up sizing.
limitations: Statement by an industry executive, not an official statistic; share of enrolment across all stages, not by grade.

title: Alef Education delivers resilient FY 2025 performance with revenues of AED 769.5 million (press release via Zawya)
key_findings: FY2025 revenue AED 769.5M (+1.4%), EBITDA margin 71.6%, net profit AED 481.1M; zero debt; AED 135M dividend.

~73,000 UAE public-school students on the platform (Abu Dhabi); 183 UAE private schools with 122,000 paying students; ~17,000 schools and ~1.8M registered students across UAE, Indonesia and Morocco; 8 new B2B/B2G contracts worth AED 64.4M.
athar_applications: Shows UAE private schools do pay per student for digital platforms at scale; a content partnership with Alef (M3) is the realistic path to UAE public schools.
limitations: Company press release; per-student fee not disclosed; revenue split by contract not disclosed.

title: MENA Venture Capital: The H1 2026 Review (MAGNiTT)
key_findings: H1 2026 MENA VC funding US$1.35B (-22% YoY) across 214 deals (-41% YoY, fewest in five years); median deal US$2.0M, mean US$7.9M; two mega rounds = US$480M; top-10 deals = 58% of capital.
UAE US$895M (+53% YoY, 66% of MENA funding); international investor participation fell 48%; MENA investors deployed US$940M (+23%).
athar_applications: Fundraising climate in 2026 is tight for early-stage MENA startups (deal count at a five-year low) — non-dilutive programmes and revenue evidence matter more.
limitations: Public summary of a gated premium report; sector breakdown (EdTech/Gaming) not public; MAGNiTT methodology proprietary.

title: Saudi Arabia tops Middle East venture capital market with $1.7bn haul and record deal flow (Arab News, 12 Jan 2026, reporting MAGNiTT FY2025)
key_findings: MAGNiTT FY2025: MENA VC US$3.8B across 688 deals (+74% funding, +6% deals); Saudi Arabia US$1.72B (+145%) across 257 deals, first in the Middle East; UAE 231 deals.
Middle East sector leaders: fintech US$1.04B; AI-related companies US$817M (+204%); EdTech and gaming not reported in the article.
athar_applications: KSA is the most active VC market by deals — consistent with a Saudi-first commercial focus; EdTech is not among the leading funded sectors.
limitations: Secondary reporting of MAGNiTT data; definitions differ from Wamda's totals (ATH-SRC-2241).

title: Record year: MENA startups funding climbs to $7.5 billion in 2025 (Wamda, Jan 2026)
key_findings: 2025: US$7.5B raised by 647 startups (+225% YoY), of which US$4B was debt; equity excluding debt grew 77%.
Saudi Arabia US$5B (211 deals); UAE US$2B (218 startups); Egypt US$263M (89 deals); fintech US$4.4B (58%); early-stage US$1.3B across 486 deals. EdTech and gaming not broken out on the page.
athar_applications: Headline MENA funding is debt- and fintech-heavy; EdTech has no visible share — investor pitch should not rely on sector momentum.
limitations: H1+H2 figures in the article do not reconcile exactly (7.7B vs 7.5B); includes debt; differs from MAGNiTT's VC-only totals.

title: How PIF is supercharging the new golden age of gaming (PIF News, 30 Jan 2025)
key_findings: National Gaming and Esports Strategy targets: incubate 250 companies, create 39,000 jobs, contribute US$13.3B to GDP; Qiddiya gaming district aims to incubate 30 game development companies.
Savvy Games Group runs a unit with incentives for FDI, support for local entrepreneurs and training; the National Development Fund and Social Development Bank created gaming investment funds.
athar_applications: Saudi state programmes reward local game-company formation — a Saudi entity or Saudi partner is the lever for gaming-sector support.
limitations: Strategic targets, not outcomes; programme eligibility details not on this page.

title: Hamdan bin Mohammed launches Dubai Program for Gaming 2033 (Dubai Media Office, 2 Nov 2023)
key_findings: Targets: 30,000 new gaming jobs, ~US$1B GDP contribution by 2033, Dubai among top-10 global gaming cities; pillars: talent, content, technology; overseen by Dubai Future Foundation.
Commits to support developers, entrepreneurs and startups in creative industries with incubation and training.
athar_applications: A Dubai-licensed games/edutainment company fits the emirate's stated priorities — useful framing for Dubai programme applications.
limitations: Policy announcement; no grant amounts or eligibility rules.

title: GameForward accelerator programme concludes with grants for Emirati studios (Dubai Media Office, 20 May 2026)
key_findings: Run by Dubai SME (Dept of Economy and Tourism) with Dubai Culture; designed for Emirati game developers; 16 Emirati-led studios (25 founders); 3 studios received grants backed by the Mohammed Bin Rashid Fund for SMEs (amounts undisclosed); PlayStation publishing partnerships for some studios.
athar_applications: Not directly accessible to a non-Emirati-led IFZA company; relevant only via an Emirati co-founder/partner.
limitations: Grant amounts and formal eligibility not published; article inconsistent on number of PlayStation deals.

title: Hub71 Access Programme (Abu Dhabi) — eligibility and incentives
key_findings: Best suited for pre-seed to Series A startups; no sector restriction listed; at least one founder must relocate long-term and build a team in Abu Dhabi.

AED 250,000 in flexible in-kind incentives (office, housing, health insurance, licensing/visa, etc.) plus AED 250,000 cash for equity via SAFE; up to AED 250,000 top-up for high performers (more equity); 12-month programme.
Cohort 21: applications by Feb 2027, programme start Sep 2027.
athar_applications: Viable for AIJUR/ATHAR only if a founder relocates to Abu Dhabi; dilutive cash component.
limitations: Equity percentage not stated; requires Abu Dhabi presence beyond the IFZA licence.

title: in5 centres (TECOM Group) — Tech, Media, Design and Science incubators, Dubai
key_findings: Four centres: in5 Tech (Dubai Internet City), in5 Design (d3), in5 Media (Dubai Production City), in5 Science (Dubai Science Park); incubation open to early-stage idea or MVP in tech, design or media.
Benefits listed: business setup, workspace, mentorship, workshops/events, investor access; durations and costs not stated.
athar_applications: in5 Media or in5 Tech is a low-friction Dubai option for an edutainment product, but it implies a TECOM free-zone setup rather than IFZA.
limitations: Costs and terms require direct enquiry; no funding amounts.

title: Mohammed Bin Rashid Innovation Fund (UAE Ministry of Economy)
publisher: UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism
key_findings: Open to entrepreneurs of all nationalities with projects registered in the UAE; priority sectors include technology and education.

Offers an Innovation Accelerator Programme (mentoring, business model, market access, financing, recruitment) and a Guarantee Scheme to help obtain development-stage financing; page updated 14 Jan 2026.
athar_applications: A UAE-registered (IFZA) company in education technology appears within scope — candidate for non-equity financing support.
limitations: Amounts, caps and free-zone eligibility not stated; requires application.

title: TAQADAM Startup Accelerator (KAUST with SAB) — programme and eligibility
authors: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
key_findings: Teams that pass the one-month virtual bootcamp receive US$40,000 non-dilutive funding and a 6-month hybrid programme; 10 startups receive additional US$100,000 follow-on at the annual showcase.

Eligible: pre-seed to Series A with a completed MVP; all nationalities; international startups eligible if they present a plan to expand into Saudi Arabia within one year; all sectors (past cohorts include gaming); 1,000+ applications per year.
athar_applications: Best-fit non-dilutive programme for ATHAR (Dubai company, Saudi-first market) once an MVP exists — aligns with the Saudi expansion plan.
limitations: Highly competitive; requires one-week in-person session at KAUST and monthly sessions; MVP required.

title: Saudi Game Champions — second edition (MCIT / CODE announcement, 29 Sep 2025)
authors: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), Center of Digital Entrepreneurship (CODE)
key_findings: Game jam followed by a video-game incubator run by MCIT's CODE with the National Technology Development Program (with ITMAM, GameBCN, Zigzag Ventures); top 20 game-jam teams enter the incubator and showcase to publishers and investors.
No funding amounts or nationality rules stated on the announcement.
athar_applications: Route to Saudi publisher/investor exposure for a Saudi-based ATHAR team or Saudi co-founders.
limitations: Eligibility unclear; edition timing may have passed — check next call.

title: Flat6Labs launches Riyadh Seed Program to empower Saudi startups (Bridge MENA, 23 Jul 2025)
key_findings: Seed funding from US$133,000 per startup, four-month programme, applicants must reside in Saudi Arabia; ~US$64,800 in perks; 10-12 teams per cycle; deadline 16 Aug 2025.
athar_applications: Equity seed route requiring Saudi residence — relevant only after a Saudi team exists.
limitations: Secondary news; equity terms not stated; the 2025 cycle has closed.

title: Applications open for 2026-2027 WISE EdTech Accelerator (Qatar News Agency, 28 Sep 2026)
key_findings: Run by WISE (Qatar Foundation) for for-profit EdTech startups at seed or pre-Series A, past MVP with sales and user engagement, and measurable educational impact; local (Qatar) and international tracks.
Deadline 31 Oct 2026; cohort starts Jan 2027; previous (2025-26) cohort had 8 startups; funding amount not stated.
athar_applications: Education-specific accelerator that values measured impact — fits ATHAR's measurement thesis, but requires sales and engagement evidence; target the 2027-28 call after pilots.
limitations: Funding terms not public; 2026 deadline (31 Oct) is days away and ATHAR has no product yet.

title: Research, Development and Innovation Authority (RDIA), Saudi Arabia — homepage (funding programmes and national RDI priorities)
key_findings: Funding items listed: Saudi Innovation Grants Program and researchers grants (via SaudiMinds portal); national RDI priorities: Health and Wellness, Sustainable Environment and Essential Needs, Energy and Industrial Leadership, Economies of the Future.
Eligibility and amounts are not on the homepage.
athar_applications: Education games are not an explicit RDI priority; a grant would need framing under 'Economies of the Future' with a Saudi research partner — low priority.
limitations: No eligibility detail; requires portal review.

title: Abdulla Al Ghurair Foundation — official homepage (purpose and programmes)
key_findings: UAE non-profit established in 2015 to empower Emirati and Arab youth through education; works through partnerships on online learning, scholarships, upskilling/career readiness and strategic philanthropy (incl. refugee education in Jordan and Lebanon).
Press at launch (Gulf News, 2015) reported a Dh4.2 billion commitment — not restated on the homepage.
athar_applications: Potential philanthropic partner for a subsidised Arabic critical-thinking/media-literacy season for underserved youth (Jordan/Lebanon) — partnership, not equity.
limitations: No open grant calls on the homepage; focus is youth 15+ and higher education/skills, not K-12 games.

title: Queen Rania Foundation for Education and Development — official homepage
key_findings: Founded 2013; focus on Arabic reading comprehension by age 10; programmes include the Karim and Jana app series (reports 3M children reached), READ school libraries (55,000 students), Iqrali parent campaign, teacher toolkits and research.
Offers 'Partner with Us' and education-network pages; no grant or startup-funding programme listed (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Research and content partner in Jordan (evidence culture, Arabic literacy) rather than a funder of ATHAR.
limitations: Self-reported reach; early-grade focus below ATHAR's 13+ audience.

title: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Knowledge Foundation (MBRF) — official homepage (initiatives)
authors: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Knowledge Foundation
key_findings: Initiatives listed: Bil Arabi (Arabic online since 2013), Digital Knowledge Hub (free Arabic digital materials), Dubai International Program for Writing, Literacy Challenge (30M Arab youth and children by 2030 with UNESCO/UNDP), Knowledge Summit, Arab Innovation platform; MoU with Arab Federation for Digital Economy (Oct 2026).
No grant/RFP process described; partnership via contact page.
athar_applications: Distribution/visibility partner for Arabic-language knowledge content (e.g., Digital Knowledge Hub, Knowledge Summit showcase) rather than a direct funder.
limitations: No published grant mechanism.

title: Berytech concludes the Lebanon Innovate Program after 46 months (Berytech, 2 Jul 2026)
key_findings: EU-funded (~€3M) Lebanon Innovate programme concluded after 46 months (closing 29 Jun 2026), implemented by Berytech with IRALEB, IRI, EBN, LEITAT and ANIMA.
Berytech homepage (2026-10-27) advertises its ScaleSmart programme with applications 'before Nov 30'; Get Funded/Competitions sections list other calls.
athar_applications: Lebanon support is donor-programme-driven and episodic; useful for a Lebanese entity (e.g., WFK-linked) but not a reliable funding pillar.
limitations: No current grant amounts for startups; ScaleSmart terms not verified.

title: What's in Lebanon for SMEs — SME Guide Book (Ministry of Economy and Trade, 2014): Kafalat guarantee programmes
authors: Ministry of Economy and Trade (Lebanon), Enterprise Unit
publisher: Ministry of Economy and Trade, Lebanon
key_findings: Kafalat guaranteed 70-90% of SME loan principal and interest (2.5% yearly commission), with interest subsidies; programmes included Kafalat Innovative (LBP 300M ceiling) and Start-ups & Innovation (LBP 650M).
Feasibility study and cash-flow projection mandatory; individuals not eligible for Plus/Innovative.
athar_applications: Historical only: LBP-denominated ceilings were wiped out by the post-2019 currency collapse; do not plan on Kafalat without current terms.
limitations: 2014 document; pre-crisis LBP amounts are obsolete; current status of programmes not verified.

title: Equity-free funding for blockchain solutions (UNICEF Venture Fund call, deadline 10 Mar 2026)
key_findings: UNICEF Venture Fund model: equity-free funding up to US$100,000 for early-stage companies registered in a UNICEF programme country, with a commitment to open-source licensing; 12-18-month support.
This call is thematic (blockchain); education is mentioned only as an impact-measurement example.
athar_applications: Only relevant if ATHAR open-sources a component (e.g., an Arabic reasoning-assessment rubric engine) and a Lebanese/Jordanian/Egyptian entity applies to a thematic call.
limitations: Thematic calls change; the UAE is not a typical programme country; open-source requirement conflicts with proprietary content.

title: SAMA affirms commitment to exchange rate policy (Saudi Central Bank, 4 May 2020)
key_findings: SAMA reaffirmed the riyal's peg to the US dollar at the official rate of 3.75 riyals per dollar.
athar_applications: Conversion constant for SAR→USD in pricing_benchmarks.csv and the unit-economics model.
limitations: Policy statement; peg could change (no indication).

title: UAE dirham peg to the US dollar since 1997 (The National, 22 Nov 2024)
key_findings: The UAE officially pegged the dirham at 3.6725 per US dollar in November 1997.
athar_applications: Conversion constant for AED→USD.
limitations: Newspaper rather than Central Bank page (CBUAE page not fetched).

title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries — Saudi Arabia: Other taxes (VAT) and Egypt: Other taxes (VAT)
key_findings: Saudi Arabia: standard VAT rate 15% effective 1 July 2020 (page last reviewed 29 Jul 2026).

Egypt: standard VAT 14%; non-resident B2C digital service providers must complete a simplified VAT registration with the ETA (last reviewed 17 Aug 2026). UAE Federal Tax Authority VAT calculator shows 5%.
athar_applications: Net-price inputs: App Store consumer prices are VAT-inclusive (Apple computes proceeds on tax-exclusive price), so a SAR 29.99 price yields SAR 26.08 ex-VAT before commission.
limitations: Professional-services summary, not the tax authority; direct web sales (outside app stores) would make ATHAR liable for registration in some markets.

title: Apple tells developers about tax and price changes for apps and in-app purchases — Saudi Arabia VAT 5% to 15% (MacTech, 2 Sep 2020, quoting Apple developer news)
key_findings: Apple announced App Store price increases in Saudi Arabia (with Chile, Mexico, Turkey) due to the VAT increase from 5% to 15%; auto-renewable subscription prices were excluded from automatic change.
Apple: proceeds 'calculated based on the tax-exclusive price' — i.e., store prices are VAT-inclusive and commission applies after VAT is removed.
athar_applications: Formula used in the unit-economics model: net = price / (1 + VAT) × (1 − store fee).
limitations: Secondary reporting of an Apple developer notice from 2020; the original Apple news item was not fetched.

title: Saudi workforce rises to 18.2M in Q2 2025 (Argaam, reporting GASTAT labour-market statistics)
key_findings: GASTAT Q2 2025: average monthly wage SAR 11,034 for Saudi workers and SAR 3,933 for expatriate workers (all sectors).
No sector breakdown (e.g., information & communication) in the article.
athar_applications: Only official national wage anchor available to convert case-production hours into money for a Saudi-based team — used as a labelled sensitivity input, not as the cost of specialist writers/engineers.
limitations: National average across all occupations; specialist creative/tech salaries are higher; excludes employer on-costs; date format ambiguous (Jul/Oct 2025).

title: TPAY MOBILE and Vodafone Egypt launch direct carrier billing on Google Play (Communications Africa, May 2020)
key_findings: Vodafone Egypt subscribers can pay for Google Play purchases via phone bill or airtime balance through TPAY MOBILE direct carrier billing (page created 6 May 2020).
TPAY MOBILE states it operates in the UAE, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and seven other countries.
athar_applications: Android purchases in Egypt can be airtime-billed — relevant for an Egypt price tier where card ownership is low (74% of Egyptian gamers use Vodafone Cash per ATH-SRC-0719).
limitations: Trade press; no usage statistics; prepaid/postpaid coverage not specified.
